acceptance: Creating a key on the System health page shows the hand-off block; one copy action copies key + address + briefing as one text.
The block's address is the deployment the key was created on (verified on a non-production origin in tests).
GET /api/ops with no key returns the full contract and nothing else; the key is ignored and never echoed when one is sent.
The panel no longer says "Setup is manual."
ci and review-gate green at the exact head; merged under the no-taps rule.
invariants: No change to authentication strength: key format, hashing, timing-safe compare, revoked-key denial and the indistinguishable 404 stay exactly as S-2 built them. The discovery document is public static text only; it grants nothing.

No change to note validation, the rate-limit value (60/hour/key), the issues response shape, or what issue data excludes. Publication reads the same constants enforcement uses (one module), never a re-statement.

No new data exposure: the discovery document contains no issue rows, no counts, no key material, no hashes, no internal identifiers. The hand-off block carries the freshly created key only in the moment the owner hands it over; never stored, logged or re-shown.
No committed key-shaped constants in tests; tests generate throwaway keys at runtime.
Trial rules unchanged: any live exercise happens on the testing copy only; this card's merge does not itself exercise a live key.

Enabling fix, kept minimal: registering this packet made the work-index executionPackets registry 81 entries, one past the shared 80 bound validatePackets applied to it, which fails check-secrets (and CI's secret scan). The registry call gets a ledger-sized bound (500); every per-packet field keeps the tight 80 bound and stays enforced, pinned by a new case in scripts/work-session.test.mjs.
next: After this lands, the owner can create a key on the testing copy, paste the whole hand-off block to an assistant with no repo access, and watch it run a real check-up — the trial Chris described in the main chat on 2026-11-04.
outcome: Creating an AI check-up key hands over a complete package — key, this deployment's base address and a plain assistant briefing in one copy block — and a keyless discovery document at GET /api/ops lets any assistant re-learn the same contract later, so key + one paste makes a working check-up agent with no repo access and no owner translation.

risk: Public-surface risk only, and bounded: the new route is keyless by design, so it must serve static contract text and nothing else — no database access, no issue data, no key material, and it must never become an authorization oracle (it answers identically with or without a key). The refactor of ops-api.ts constants is behaviour-preserving and covered by the unchanged integration suite. AI-PR-READ-FIRST items honored: the keyless route treats no limiter as a security barrier (it needs none — it exposes nothing and writes nothing), and authorization stays deny-by-default on the data endpoints, untouched.
